subject: biology
title: Sex Linkage & Mutations Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll trace sex-linked traits and meet the four main classes of mutation.
meta_desc: A-Level Biology Genetics — sex linkage on the X chromosome, substitution, insertion, deletion and frameshift mutations.
final_note: You learned that sex-linked recessives like haemophilia affect males more, and that substitutions can be silent/missense/nonsense while indels can shift the reading frame.

concepts.def: Trait carried on a sex chromosome — usually the X
Heterozygous for X-linked recessive — unaffected but passes allele
One base swapped for another — silent, missense or nonsense
One or more bases added — often causes frameshift
One or more bases removed — often causes frameshift
Indel shifts reading frame, changing every downstream codon

walkthroughs.body_html:
Females are XX, males are XY.

The Y is much smaller and carries few genes. Genes only on X show sex linkage.

Examples: haemophilia and red-green colour blindness.

Females have two X — recessive can be masked. Males only have one X — recessive always expressed → males more often affected.

Use H for normal, h for haemophilia (X-linked recessive).

Carrier mother X^H X^h × normal father X^H Y →

- X^H X^H (normal girl)
- X^H X^h (carrier girl)
- X^H Y (normal boy)
- X^h Y (haemophilic boy)

So 50% of sons affected, 50% of daughters carriers.

Substitution — one base swapped. Effects:
- Silent — same amino acid (degenerate code)
- Missense — different amino acid
- Nonsense — premature stop codon

Insertion / deletion — adds/removes bases. If number ≠ multiple of 3 → frameshift: every codon downstream is misread.

Result: protein usually non-functional.

mcqs.q: Why are X-linked recessive disorders more common in males than females?
options: Males have more X chromosomes
Males only have one X — no second allele to mask the recessive
The Y chromosome carries extra copies
Females cannot inherit X-linked alleles

mcqs.q: Which type of mutation causes a frameshift?
options: Silent substitution
Missense substitution
Insertion of 1 base
Insertion of 3 bases

mcqs.q: Why are X-linked recessive conditions more common in males?
options: X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.
Males have only one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed — there's no second X to mask it.
X-linked recessive conditions affect more males because the Y chromosome makes the disease worse.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.

mcqs.q: What does it mean for an allele to be 'dominant'?
options: It is expressed in the phenotype when at least one copy is present (in a heterozygote).
X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.
A dominant allele is the most common allele in a population.
A dominant allele physically destroys the recessive allele in the genome.

mcqs.q: Why are frameshift mutations usually more severe than point substitutions?
options: X-linked conditions affect only males because females cannot inherit X-linked alleles.
Frameshift mutations are usually silent because cells can correct them.
Frameshifts only change the codon at the site of the mutation, like a substitution.
Insertions/deletions of a non-multiple of 3 shift the reading frame, changing every codon downstream of the mutation.
